text:
HR@10 against 99 fixed unique negatives measures success within 100-item candidate sets. Fixed users/candidates enable reproducible, paired comparisons, but do not remove sampling bias: sampled metrics can reverse full-catalog model rankings even in expectation ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). With 200 users/category, one changed hit moves category HR by 0.005 and four-category macro HR by 0.00125. Repeatedly choosing architectures, hyperparameters or checkpoints on these same users risks optimistic selection and adaptive overfitting; fixed seeds do not prevent this ([Dwork et al.](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html)).

For this design, use a category-stratified paired user bootstrap: record each user's hit difference between two models; resample 200 users with replacement within each category, preserving model pairing and each user's candidates. In every replicate compute the four category mean differences, then their equally weighted average; derive the macro interval from that replicate distribution, rather than averaging category interval endpoints. Pairing requires identical resampled indices across models ([SciPy documentation](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html)). Report category effects alongside the macro effect. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on trained models, observed candidate sets and these four categories; it excludes training-seed/candidate-resampling uncertainty and does not correct adaptive selection. Preserve shared-user clustering across categories if applicable.

Consequently, gains support only better observed sampled validation performance under the pinned protocol. They do not establish full-catalog HR@10, generalization to new categories, online utility or an adaptive-forgetting mechanism. Forgetting claims require controlled ablations and temporal or history-perturbation evidence; aggregate HR gains alone cannot distinguish selective forgetting from recency weighting, regularization or optimization effects. Keep these limitations explicit without changing the evaluator or accessing held-out tests.
